rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poetic praise calls people the sun, moon, or light, illustrating figurative use of light for honor and distinction.
rows.anchor: فإنك شمس والملوك كواكب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may be called light as praise because He brings things into being and all their light derives from Him; sensory radiance and brilliance imply createdness and are denied of God.
rows.anchor: الله سبحانه نور من جهة المدح لأنه واجد الأشياء ونور جميع الأشياء منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One should not address God simply as Light or Originator without an appended complement; divine names and attributes follow transmitted wording.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يقال: لله يا نور إلا أن يضم إليه شيء كما لا يجوز

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali read the opening as a verb, meaning that God illuminates the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: قرأ علي بن أبي طالب: الله نور السماوات والأرض على الفعل

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some take the pronoun in His light as the believer's light, with faith and Quran placed in the believer's heart.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم: هي عائدة الى المؤمن أي مثل نوره

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy explains that God first mentioned His own light and then the believer's light in the parable.
rows.anchor: روى الربيع عن أبي العالية عن أبي بن كعب في هذه الآية قال:

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy's recitation makes the referent explicit as the light of whoever believes in God.
rows.anchor: وهكذا كان يقرأ أبي: مثل نور من آمن به

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وزيد بن أسلم وابنه
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, Zayd ibn Aslam, and his son identify the light as the Quran.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والحسن وزيد بن أسلم وابنه: أراد بالنور القرآن

rows.speaker: كعب وسعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Ka'b and Sa'id ibn Jubayr identify the light as Muhammad; Muqatil transmits the same view from al-Dahhak, with the lights attributed to God as an honor.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب وسعيد بن جبير: هو محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ومثله روى مقاتل عن الضحاك

rows.speaker: عطية عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Atiyya transmits from Ibn Abbas that the light means obedience, which God calls His light and then illustrates with a parable.
rows.anchor: وروى عطية عن ابن عباس قال: يعني بالنور الطاعة

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: The People of Meaning call the construction inverted, as if it said a lamp in a niche; a niche is a recess without an opening, and the word also named a container, including a leather vessel for cooling water.
rows.anchor: قال أهل المعاني: هذا من المقلوب أي كمصباح في مشكوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An anonymous poet's comparison of eyes to niches in stone supplies a usage example for the word mishkat.
rows.anchor: كأن عينيه مشكاتان في حجر … قيضا اقتياضا بأطراف المناقير

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some explain the niche as the column of a lamp that holds its wick.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المشكوة: عمود القنديل الذي فيه الفتيلة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid calls the niche a lamp containing a misbah; misbah derives from light, as do words for morning and a bright-faced person.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: هي القنديل فيها مصباح أي سراج وأصله من الضوء

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil says misbah means the lamp itself; others say siraj is larger, since scripture calls the sun a siraj and other stars lamps.
rows.anchor: فقال الخليل: المصباح : نفس السراج وقيل: السراج أعظم من المصباح

rows.speaker: أبو أسيد
rows.claim: Abu Asid reports the Prophet's instruction to eat olive oil and use it on the body because it comes from a blessed tree.
rows.anchor: عن أبي أسيد قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن ثابت الأنصاري
rows.claim: Abdullah ibn Thabit al-Ansari urged his sons to oil their heads, striking them with a staff when they refused the oil used by the Prophet.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الطفيل عن عبد الله بن ثابت الأنصاري

rows.speaker: عقبة بن عامر
rows.claim: Uqba ibn Amir reports the Prophet's recommendation of olive oil as a remedy, including for hemorrhoids.
rows.anchor: عن عقبة بن عامر أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «عليكم بهذه الشجرة المباركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oil nearly shines from its purity and brightness; without fire touching it means before any fire reaches it.
rows.anchor: يكاد زيتها يضيء من صفائه وضيائه. ولو لم تمسسه نار قيل: أن تصيبه نار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars disagree over what the parable represents and whom its niche, glass, and lamp signify.
rows.anchor: واختلف العلماء في معنى هذا المثل والممثل وفي المعني بالمشكاة والزجاجة والمصباح

rows.speaker: كعب الأحبار
rows.claim: Ka'b tells Ibn Abbas that the parable is Muhammad: the niche is his chest, glass his heart, lamp his prophethood, and the tree the tree of prophecy; his prophetic light and message would show even without speech.
rows.anchor: فقال كعب: هذا مثل ضربه الله سبحانه لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، فالمشكاة صدره

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar reports that the niche is Muhammad's interior, the glass his heart, and the lamp God's light in him; neither east nor west means neither Jew nor Christian, while the tree is Abraham and light upon light links Abraham's and Muhammad's hearts.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر في هذه الآية قال: المشكاة جوف محمد، والزجاجة قلبه، والمصباح النور

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b maps the niche to Abraham, the glass to Ishmael, and the lamp to Muhammad; Abraham is the blessed tree because most prophets descend from him, and neither east nor west means he was neither Jew nor Christian but an upright Muslim.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب القرظي: المشكاة إبراهيم، والزجاجة إسماعيل، المصباح محمد

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b says Muhammad's fine qualities seemed ready to shine before revelation, while light upon light means a prophet descended from a prophet.
rows.anchor: يعني تكاد محاسن محمد تظهر للناس قبل أن أوحي إليه نور على نور أي نبي من نسل نبي

rows.speaker: مقاتل عن الضحاك
rows.claim: Muqatil transmits from al-Dahhak that Abd al-Muttalib is the niche, Abdullah the glass, and Muhammad the lamp; the olive tree is Meccan because Mecca is the world's center.
rows.anchor: وروى مقاتل عن الضحاك قال: شبه عبد المطلب بالمشكاة وعبد الله بالزجاجة والنبي

rows.speaker: بعض البلغاء
rows.claim: An eloquent writer describes the tree allegorically: its root is prophecy, branch is manliness, branches are revelation, leaves are interpretation, and attendants are Gabriel and Michael.
rows.anchor: ووصف بعض البلغاء هذه الشجرة فقال: هي شجرة التقى والرضوان

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Ka'b says the parable is the believer: the niche is the self, the glass the breast, and the lamp the faith and Quran God put in the heart.
rows.anchor: روى الربيع بن أنس عن أبي العالية عن أبي بن كعب قال: هذا مثل المؤمن

words: فِى بُيُوتٍ أَذِنَ ٱللَّهُ أَن تُرْفَعَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may attach the lamp to houses, or mean that it is kindled in houses, which most commentators identify as mosques.
rows.anchor: ذلك المصباح في بيوت ويجوز أن يكون معناه: توقد في بيوت وهي المساجد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says mosques are God's houses on earth and shine for the inhabitants of heaven as stars shine for earthly people.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: المساجد بيوت الله عز وجل في الأرض، وهي تضيء لأهل السماء

rows.speaker: عمرو بن ميمون
rows.claim: Amr ibn Maymun says the Prophet's Companions held mosques to be God's houses and that God honors those who visit them.
rows.anchor: وقال عمرو بن ميمون: أدركت أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهم يقولون: المساجد بيوت الله

rows.speaker: ابن أبي بريدة
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Burayda identifies four mosques built only by prophets: the Kaaba by Abraham and Ishmael, Jerusalem by David and Solomon, and the Medina and Quba mosques by Muhammad.
rows.anchor: عن ابن أبي بريدة في قوله سبحانه في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع الآية. قال: إنما هي أربع مساجد

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Anas and Burayda report that the Prophet identified the houses as those of prophets and affirmed that Ali and Fatima's house was among the most excellent of them.
rows.anchor: قالا: قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هذه الآية في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع ويذكر فيها اسمه

rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq identifies the houses as the houses of the Prophet.
rows.anchor: الصادق: بيوت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the houses are Medina.
rows.anchor: السدي: المدينة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers mosques because the context describes houses built for prayer and worship.
rows.anchor: وأولى الأقوال بالصواب أنها المساجد لدلالة سياق الآية على أنها بيوت بنيت للصلاة

rows.speaker: قائل
rows.claim: An objection asks why the niche and lamp are singular while the houses are plural.
rows.anchor: فإن قيل: ما الوجه في توحيده المشكاة والمصباح وجمع البيوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One answer calls this a shift in address that begins with singular and ends with plural, as in the address to the Prophet followed by plural divorce wording.
rows.anchor: قلنا: هذا من الخطاب المتلون الذي يفتح بالتوحيد ويختم بالجمع كقوله سبحانه يا أيها النبي إذا طلقتم النساء

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another answer says the singular referents recur individually in each house.
rows.anchor: وقيل: رجع الى كل واحد من البيوت

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A further answer compares the wording to saying the moon is in the heavens, although it is in only one of them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو مثل قوله سبحانه وجعل القمر فيهن نورا وإنما هو في واحدة منها

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses raised as built, comparing the phrase with Abraham and Ishmael raising the foundations of the House.
rows.anchor: أن ترفع أي تبنى عن مجاهد نظيره قوله سبحانه وإذ يرفع إبراهيم القواعد من البيت وإسماعيل

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan interprets raised as honored or magnified.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: تعظيم، ويذكر فيها اسمه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says God's Book is recited in the houses.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يتلى فيها كتابه

rows.speaker: قتادة وأشهب العقيلي ونصر بن عاصم الليثي وابن عامر وعاصم
rows.claim: Qatada, Ashhab al-Uqayli, Nasr ibn Asim, Ibn Amir, and Asim read yusabbaḥu with fatḥa on the ba and without naming the agent.
rows.anchor: قرأ قتادة وأشهب العقيلي ونصر بن عاصم الليثي وابن عامر وعاصم بفتح الباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the passive reading, men is supplied as the delayed agent; the pause falls at evenings. Other readers use the active, making glorification the men's action.
rows.anchor: والوقف على هذه القراءة عند قوله والآصال. وقرأ الآخرون بكسر الباء جعلوا التسبيح فعلا للرجال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says every occurrence of tasbih in the Quran means prayer, as indicated here by dawn and evenings.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كل تسبيح في القرآن صلاة

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators understand the obligatory prayers: dawn is Fajr, while the plural evenings include Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, and Isha because asil covers them all.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: أراد الصلوات المفروضة، فالصلاة التي تؤدى بالغدو صلاة الفجر

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that whoever regularly goes to the mosque morning and evening, preferring it, receives a prepared welcome and reward in Paradise for each visit.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «ما من أحد يغدو ويروح إلى المسجد

rows.speaker: سهل بن سعد الساعدي
rows.claim: Sahl ibn Sa'd reports that one who goes to the mosque to learn or teach good is like a returning victorious fighter, while one going for another purpose sees worshippers without belonging to them.
rows.anchor: عن سهل بن سعد الساعدي قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من غدا الى المسجد وراح ليتعلم خيرا

rows.speaker: قائل
rows.claim: One explanation singles out men because women are not obligated to attend Friday or congregational prayers in mosques.
rows.anchor: قيل: وجه تخصيص الرجال بالذكر في هذه البيوت أنه ليس على النساء جمعة ولا جماعة

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: The People of Meaning say commerce is singled out because it is the greatest distraction from prayers and other acts of devotion.
rows.anchor: قال أهل المعاني: إنما خص التجارات لأنها أعظم ما يشتغل بها الإنسان عن الصلوات

rows.speaker: الواقدي
rows.claim: In answer to why sale is named alongside trade, al-Waqidi says trade here means purchase, as in the verse about seeing trade.
rows.anchor: فالجواب عنه ما قال الواقدي أنه أراد بالتجارة الشراء نظيره قوله سبحانه وإذا رأوا تجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iqamat al-salat drops its final h in annexation: the suffix originally compensates for deleted waw in the form aqwama, whose waw was dropped after a heavy vowel and transferred to qaf; annexation then replaces the h, as with ida and zina.
rows.anchor: لأن أصل الكلمة أقومت إقواما فاستثقلوا الضمة على الواو فسكنوها فاجتمع حرفان ساكنان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A line by al-A'sha supports dropping the h from idda when the noun is annexed: the phrase means the appointed term of what they promised.
rows.anchor: كقول الشاعر: إن الخليط أجدوا البين وانجردوا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan takes the zakat here to mean the obligatory alms.
rows.anchor: وإيتاء الزكاة المفروضة عن الحسن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets zakat as sincere obedience to God.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الزكاة إخلاص الطاعة لله سبحانه وتعالى

rows.speaker: ابن حيان
rows.claim: Ibn Hayyan identifies the men as the People of the Suffa.
rows.anchor: قال ابن حيان: هم أهل الصفة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses Tabaraka as having brought every blessing.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، كأن معناه: جاء بكل بركة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says blessing comes from God.
rows.anchor: دليله قول الحسن: تجيء البركة من قبله

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses Tabaraka as exalted or greatly elevated.
rows.anchor: الضحاك: تعظم، الخليل: تمجد، وأصل البركة النماء

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil glosses Tabaraka as glorified; the root baraka means growth and increase.
rows.anchor: الضحاك: تعظم، الخليل: تمجد، وأصل البركة النماء والزيادة

rows.speaker: المحققون
rows.claim: The verifying scholars say the attribute means eternally established and enduring; baraka originally means stability, as in a bird settling on water or a camel kneeling.
rows.anchor: وقال المحققون: معنى هذه الصفة ثبت ودام بما لم يزل ولا يزال، وأصل البركة الثبوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One says Tabaraka Allah, but not mutabarak or mubarak of God, because divine names and attributes are limited to revealed formulations.
rows.anchor: ويقال: تبارك الله ولا يقال لله متبارك أو مبارك لأنه ينتهى في صفاته وأسمائه الى حيث ورد التوقيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Furqan is the Quran, God's servant is Muhammad, the worlds comprise jinn and humans, and the revelation warns them.
rows.anchor: الذي نزل الفرقان القرآن على عبده محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ليكون للعالمين الجن والإنس نذيرا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the warner is the Quran.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم: النذير هو القرآن

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view identifies the warner as Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God owns heaven and earth, took neither child nor partner, created everything that can be called created, and measured, formed, and equipped each thing for its proper use without flaw or disparity.
rows.anchor: وخلق كل شيء مما يطلق له صفة المخلوق فقدره تقديرا فسواه وهيأه لما يصلح له، فلا خلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following verse refers to idol worshippers who took gods besides God that create nothing and are themselves created.
rows.anchor: واتخذوا يعني عبدة الأوثان من دونه آلهة لا يخلقون شيئا وهم يخلقون

rows.speaker: النضر بن الحارث وأصحابه
rows.claim: The disbelievers are identified as al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and his companions, who alleged Muhammad fabricated the Quran and was assisted by others; Mujahid identifies those helpers as Jews, while al-Hasan ibn Ubayd ibn al-Hadr says an Abyssinian soothsayer.
rows.anchor: يعني النضر بن الحرث وأصحابه إن هذا ما هذا القرآن إلا إفك افتراه

rows.speaker: جبر ويسار وعداس
rows.claim: A further view identifies Muhammad's alleged helpers as Jabr, Yasar, and Addas, a client of Huwaytib ibn Abd al-Uzza.
rows.anchor: جبر ويسار وعداس مولى حويطب بن عبد العزى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The charge is injustice and falsehood because they attributed God's speech to fabrication and a lie.
rows.anchor: فقد جاؤ يعني ما يلي هذه المقالة ظلما وزورا بنسبتهم كلام الله سبحانه الى الإفك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They also claimed these were ancient fables he had copied down, dictated to him morning and evening.
rows.anchor: أيضا أساطير الأولين اكتتبها فهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God refutes them: the Quran was sent down by the One who knows the secrets of the heavens and earth, who is forgiving and merciful.
rows.anchor: قل أنزله الذي يعلم السر في السماوات والأرض إنه كان غفورا رحيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They object that Muhammad eats and works in markets like them, and ask for an angel to confirm him, treasure so he need not seek livelihood, or a garden to eat from.
rows.anchor: وقالوا مال هذا الرسول يعنون محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم يأكل الطعام كما نأكل ويمشي في الأسواق

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
rows.claim: Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Khalaf read the garden phrase with the first-person plural nun, we eat, instead of the general reading's third-person ya.
rows.anchor: هذه قراءة العامة، وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف بالنون أي نأكل نحن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusation that the Messenger is bewitched was revealed concerning the story of Ibn Abi Umayya, previously recounted in the Bani Isra'il sura.
rows.anchor: وقال الظالمون إن تتبعون إلا رجلا مسحورا نزلت هذه الآية في قصة ابن أبي أمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers stray from guidance and have no way out of misguidance, remaining ignorant and turning from right judgment despite being obliged to accept the truth.
rows.anchor: فضلوا فلا يستطيعون سبيلا إلى الهدى ومخرجا من الضلالة فأخبر الله أنهم متمسكون بالجهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their case proves that the capacity by which misguidance occurs differs from the capacity through which guidance and faith are attained.
rows.anchor: فثبت أن الاستطاعة التي بها الضلال غير الاستطاعة التي يحصل بها الهدى والإيمان

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid takes the promised better gift to mean better than what the disbelievers demanded.
rows.anchor: تبارك الذي إن شاء جعل لك خيرا من ذلك أي مما قالوا، عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ikrima transmits from Ibn Abbas that it means better than walking markets and seeking a livelihood: gardens with rivers and fortified houses; qasr relates to preventing access.
rows.anchor: وروى عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال: يعني خيرا من المشي في الأسواق والتماس المعاش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A palace is a fortified dwelling; the word qasr derives from restraint or barring access.
rows.anchor: أي بيوتا مشيدة، وسمي قصرا لأنه قصر أي حبس ومنع من الوصول إليه

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وابن عامر وعاصم
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, and Asim in Abu Bakr and al-Mufaddal's transmissions read yaj'alu with a nominative lām; the others make it jussive, coordinated with the conditional result after if He wills.
rows.anchor: واختلف القراء في قوله ويجعل فرفع لامه ابن كثير وابن عامر وعاصم برواية أبي بكر والمفضل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that after polytheists mocked the Prophet's poverty, he grieved and Gabriel came to console him, reminding him that earlier messengers also ate and worked in markets.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: لما عير المشركون رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالفاقة فقالوا: مال هذا الرسول

rows.speaker: النخعي ومجاهد
rows.claim: Al-Nakha'i and Mujahid take mahjur from hajr, bad speech: the people said false things about the Quran, calling it magic, poetry, and tales.
rows.anchor: وقال الرسول يعني ويقول الرسول في ذلك اليوم يا رب إن قومي اتخذوا هذا القرآن مهجورا أي قالوا فيه غير الحق

rows.speaker: الآخرون
rows.claim: Others derive mahjur from abandonment: they turned away from the Quran, neither believing in it nor acting by it.
rows.anchor: وقال الآخرون: هو من الهجران أي أعرضوا عنه وتركوه فلم يؤمنوا به ولم يعملوا

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas reports that a person who learns and teaches Quran but leaves a mushaf unattended will face it on Judgment Day, when it asks God to judge between them for being abandoned.
rows.anchor: حدثنا أنس بن مالك قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من تعلم القرآن وعلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Just as God made enemies among Muhammad's polytheist people, He made every prophet enemies among the criminals of his own people; Muhammad should be patient, as God will guide and support him.
rows.anchor: وكما جعلنا لك يا محمد أعداء ومن مشركي قومك كذلك جعلنا لكل نبي عدوا من المجرمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression parses the Lord as specification and guide/supporter as circumstantial predicates.
rows.anchor: وكفى بربك هاديا ونصيرا على الحال والتمييز

words: لَوْلَا نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقُرْءَانُ جُمْلَةًۭ وَٰحِدَةًۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers ask why the Quran was not sent all at once, like the Torah, Psalms, and Gospel; God says gradual revelation strengthens Muhammad's heart so he can absorb and retain it.
rows.anchor: وقال الذين كفروا لولا نزل عليه على محمد القرآن جملة واحدة كما أنزلت التوراة على موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier prophets could read and write, but Muhammad was unlettered; the Quran also contains abrogating and abrogated material and answers questions, so portions were separated to help him retain it and people receive it.
rows.anchor: فإن الكتب نزلت على أنبياء يكتبون ويقرءون، والقرآن أنزل على نبي أمي ولأن من القرآن الناسخ والمنسوخ

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses rattalnahu as sending it in successive portions.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ورسلناه ترسيلا

rows.speaker: النخعي والحسن
rows.claim: Al-Nakha'i and al-Hasan say the Quran was divided verse by verse and thing by thing over about twenty-three years.
rows.anchor: وقال النخعي والحسن: فرقناه تفريقا آية بعد آية وشيئا بعد شيء، وكان بين أوله وآخره نحو ثلاث وعشرين سنة

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses tartil as making the Quran's meaning clear and explaining it.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: وفسرناه تفسيرا، والترتيل: التبيين في ترسل وتثبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whenever the disbelievers offer an argument against Muhammad, God gives him the truth to answer and refute it with the best explanation and detail.
rows.anchor: ولا يأتونك يا محمد يعني هؤلاء المشركين بمثل في إبطال أمرك إلا جئناك بالحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those dragged to Hell on their faces will have the worst place and be furthest astray.
rows.anchor: الذين يعني هم الذين يحشرون على وجوههم فيساقون ويجرون إلى جهنم أولئك شر مكانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham asks to join the prophets before him in rank and station; Ibn Abbas instead explains the request as joining the people of Paradise.
rows.anchor: وألحقني بالصالحين بمن قبلي من النبيين في الدرجة والمنزلة. وقال ابن عباس: بأهل الجنة.

words: وَٱجْعَل لِّى لِسَانَ صِدْقٍۢ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham asks for beautiful remembrance, praise, and broad acceptance among later peoples; God granted it, and religious communities honor him and build upon his legacy.
rows.anchor: أي ذكرا جميلا وثناء حسنا وقبولا عاما في الأمم

rows.speaker: القتيبي
rows.claim: Al-Qutaybi says tongue stands metaphorically for speech, which is alluded to by the tongue, and Arabs also call a language a tongue; al-A'sha al-Bahili's line uses lisan for a message or speech.
rows.anchor: قال القتيبي: ووضع اللسان موضع القول على الاستعارة لأن القول يكنى بها

rows.speaker: الأعشى الباهلي
rows.claim: Al-A'sha al-Bahili's verse uses lisan for a spoken message that arrives from a distant source.
rows.anchor: وقال أعشى باهلة: إني أتتني لسان لا أسر بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author points back to his explanation in Surah al-Tawba of why Abraham sought forgiveness for his father.
rows.anchor: وقد بينا المعنى الذي من أجله استغفر إبراهيم (عليه السلام) لأبيه في سورة التوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran is revelation from the Lord of the worlds, brought by the Trustworthy Spirit to Muhammad's heart so he receives it and warns in clear Arabic.
rows.anchor: وإنه لتنزيل رب العالمين يعني القرآن

rows.speaker: الحجازيون وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: The Hijaz readers and Abu Amr read the verb lightly with nominative al-Ruh al-Amin, meaning Gabriel descended with the Quran.
rows.anchor: قرأ الحجازيون وأبو عمر بتخفيف الزاي ورفع الحاء والنون يعنون جبرئيل (عليه السلام) بالقرآن

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد وأبو حاتم
rows.claim: Other readers use the doubled verb with accusative pronoun, meaning the Spirit brought it down; Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim prefer this reading because تنزيل is the verbal noun of nazzala.
rows.anchor: وهو اختيار أبي عبيد وأبي حاتم لقوله وإنه لتنزيل

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators take the pronoun to mean the Quran's mention and account in the books of earlier peoples.
rows.anchor: وإنه يعني ذكر القرآن وخبره عن أكثر المفسرين

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says the reference is to the mention and description of Muhammad in earlier scriptures.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: يعني ذكر محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ونعته لفي زبر كتب الأولين

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-A'mash reads zubur with a quiescent ba; other readers use the vowelled form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش زبر بجزم الباء، وغيره بالرفع

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn Amir reads ayatan in the nominative, while the other readers put it in the accusative.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر تكن بالتاء آية بالرفع، غيره تكن بالتاء آية بالنصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse asks whether it is not a sign for the deniers that scholars of the Children of Israel recognize Muhammad.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الآية أو لم يكن لهؤلاء المنكرين دلالة وعلامة أن يعلمه يعني محمدا علماء بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Meccans asked Jews in Medina about Muhammad; they said his time had come and that the Torah described him, which was a sign of his truthfulness.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: بعث أهل مكة الى اليهود وهم بالمدينة فسألوهم عن محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالوا: إن هذا لزمانه
